geopolitics_summary: Marine heat waves threaten European nuclear cooling; US–Iran sanctions tighten; Russia's Rosatom faces EU safety scrutiny amid Hungary plant construction.

themes.headline: Hungary nuclear plant cooling constrained by low Danube water levels
themes.why_it_matters: Danube heat-driven low water reduces nuclear output capacity. Directly pressures EU baseload; forces fuel-switching to gas/coal and lifts day-ahead and Cal+1 power spreads across Central Europe.

themes.headline: Marine heat waves across Europe reduce nuclear and hydro plant cooling
themes.why_it_matters: Continent-wide ocean/air temperature anomalies constrain thermal plant dispatch and hydro inflows. Reduces available capacity, tightens power curve; affects EUA via higher dispatch carbon and spot–forward spreads.

themes.headline: US natural gas production set to reach record 122.5 Bcf/d in 2026
themes.why_it_matters: Higher US LNG export capacity from record natgas production increases LNG supply to global markets. Reduces LNG arb spreads (US Henry Hub–TTF), pressures European gas prices and power; weakens power via cheaper gas fuel-switching.

themes.headline: Russia's Rosatom accused of nuclear safety violations in EU-tied projects
themes.why_it_matters: Ukraine seeks EU sanctions on Rosatom; Hungary's Paks II expansion uses same tech as Egypt's El Dabaa. Regulatory risk to future nuclear capacity; sanctions could disrupt EU nuclear supply chains and force capacity delays, raising power costs.

themes.headline: Iran economic isolation may not achieve US production-cut goals
themes.why_it_matters: Escalating Iran sanctions risk fail to cut crude supply if Tehran absorbs economic pressure. Indirect: crude-to-gas switching economics and global LNG arbs affect European TTF/power via feedstock competition and displacement.
